text:
morgan: quick spike from a customer: their chat widget cold-starts show a 70ms penalty on first token due to shard reads. thinking about a 'selective layer warmstart' approach that only brings up the minimal set of KV chunks needed for first N tokens. anyone experimented with this?
elaine: we've done something similar internally for large-batch jobs, but never micro-granular for single-request latency. main challenge is deciding what to prefetch without overfetching.
chao: one idea: offline profiling per model -> generate 'hotspot fingerprints' per model family. At runtime we map incoming prompt features (hashed, local-only) to a fingerprint ID and ask the node to prefetch the listed shards/layer-slices.
morgan: love that. how do we represent it in manifests so bundles are portable?
elaine: propose adding a `warmstart_buckets` top-level optional key in model bundle manifests. each bucket is an ID with an opaque score vector and a compact list of (shard_id, chunk_range, estimated_bytes). Eg:```json
"warmstart_buckets": {
  "bskt:7f3a": {
    "description": "short-system-instructions",
    "list": [
      {"shard": 0, "chunks": "0..3", "bytes": "12000"},
      {"shard": 5, "chunks": "1..2", "bytes": "8000"}
    ]
  }
}
```
chao: note: keep bucket IDs short and opaque. Do not embed example prompts. Only store aggregate stats. This avoids PII and helps with enterprise compliance.
morgan: runtime contract? Should router include a header like `X-Warmstart-Bucket: bskt:7f3a` or `X-Warmstart-Eligibility: allow`?
elaine: router sends `Warmstart-Bucket: bskt:7f3a` only when the fingerprint lookup is permitted by the tenant policy. Node checks local cache, fires async prefetch for `high` priority items and continues with index-first fallback for anything missing.
chao: important: prefetch must be best-effort and cancellable if request completes or times out. Also limit concurrent warmstart bytes per node to avoid thrashing.
morgan: telemetry we should collect: `ws_bucket_lookup` (id or null), `ws_prefetch_bytes`, `ws_latency_delta_ms`, and `ws_decision` (prefetch/skipped/opted_out). Add tenant-level opt-out too.
elaine: + governance: retention of fingerprint maps should be configurable and default to ephemeral (e.g., 7 days) for hosted. For private deployments, the map stays local and retired per tenant policy.
chao: thought on registry: keep profile registry in a config-service. For hosted API, profile lookup returns either the bucket ID or 404. Avoid embedding full lists in headers. Nodes fetch bucket content lazily and cache it. For air-gapped installs, registry runs inside VPC.
morgan: fallback plan: if bucket lookup fails, do nothing special and rely on existing index-first path. We should ensure no hard dependency.
elaine: risks: wrong bucket increases IO and might hurt tail latency. mitigation: threshold-based enablement: only enable for buckets where historical savings > X ms and bytes overhead < Y. Also stage behind feature flag.
chao: can we make this model-format-agnostic? hot buckets point to shard IDs and chunk ranges; for formats that don't shard similarly, we can map at upload time to the bundle's internal addressing.
morgan: ok. next steps: elaine to write an RFC for `warmstart_buckets` schema + registry API; chao to draft runtime limits and telemetry metrics; i'll sketch a small PoC on staging and run microbench A/B for chat widget workloads.
ops-bot: note created: eng-ml/boards -> "ws-buckets-rfc" assigned to elaine, chao.
elaine: I'll include a sample registry API: `GET /profiles/:model_id/:fingerprint -> {bucket: "bskt:7f3a"}` and `GET /buckets/:id -> {list:[...]}`. Keep responses compact and cacheable.
chao: also add an access-control header so tenants can disable lookups: `X-Warmstart-Allow: false` in account profile.
morgan: thanks all. trying to be conservative here: enable only for models and tenants opted into beta. sound good?
elaine: yes. i'll aim to land RFC draft by EOW.
chao: i'll run a quick sim next week and post numbers. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
